name: dbt Core
summary: A project-oriented transformation engine that compiles declarative SQL resources into a dependency-ordered warehouse build graph with adapter-specific materializations and tests.

features.name: Declarative resource graph
features.description: A dbt project declares resources such as models, sources, snapshots, seeds, tests, macros, and exposures; ref-based dependencies determine the order of model execution and form a DAG.
benefits: Makes transformation dependencies inspectable and schedulable
Allows SQL files and project metadata to serve as a reproducible build description
costs: The graph must remain acyclic and complete enough for dbt to infer ordering
Warehouse behavior outside declared resources can remain outside the graph

features.name: Adapter-mediated warehouse execution
features.description: dbt delegates warehouse-specific relation creation and SQL execution to adapters while retaining a common project and resource model.
benefits: Reuses project-level transformation concepts across supported data platforms
Localizes platform-specific SQL and DDL behavior at an adapter boundary
costs: Cross-platform behavior depends on adapter capabilities and SQL differences
The common abstraction cannot erase warehouse-specific performance and transaction semantics

features.name: Configurable model materialization
features.description: dbt persists models using configurable strategies including views, tables, incremental models, ephemeral CTE expansion, and materialized views where supported.
benefits: Lets one logical model target different freshness, cost, and query-latency profiles
Supports incremental rebuilds when full recomputation is too expensive
costs: Each strategy changes freshness, storage, rebuild, and debugging behavior
Incremental and platform-managed strategies require additional configuration and platform support

mathematical_views.model: Finite dependency DAG and topological execution order
mathematical_views.question: How does dbt turn references between resources into an executable order that respects upstream dependencies?
assumptions: Declared ref and source relationships form an acyclic graph
A topological order is sufficient for the selected build operation
External warehouse changes and concurrent execution effects are abstracted

mathematical_views.question: How can a logical SQL transformation be viewed separately from the warehouse relation used to persist its result?
assumptions: The adapter implements the selected materialization contract
The materialized relation preserves the intended query semantics for the modeled scope
Cost, freshness, and warehouse-specific behavior are explicit trade-offs rather than algebraic equivalences

benefits: Dependency-aware builds and lineage-oriented project structure
costs: Undeclared side effects and cycles undermine graph-based planning

benefits: Portable project concepts across warehouse adapters
costs: Portability is bounded by adapter feature and SQL dialect differences

benefits: Workload-specific balance of freshness, query speed, and build cost
costs: Materialization choices create different operational and debugging obligations
